analysis:
Examined the new IPC reference, configuration metadata and patch, and both BASE configuration excerpts. These documentation changes describe a new local availability-control surface, not a demonstrated implementation vulnerability. docs/reference/addon-hold-ipc.md:21–23,34–36,54–59 specify private files, bounded framing/connections, persistent leases, identifier-scoped operations and a lock that can extend holds beyond expiry. Lines 75–96 specify per-request audit-token code authentication, same-UID checks, Apple-anchored signer identity and hardened runtime, with DEBUG-only identity expansion; they explicitly disclaim protection against the owning user. Configuration's added section (patch HEAD 150–164) documents socket relocation, lease/drain bounds and exclusion of overrides from LaunchAgent passthrough. No supplied change exposes prompt plaintext, keys, serving credentials, billing data or changes cache cryptography/scoping (A-001, A-003, A-008, T-041), nor establishes an attestation/authorization bypass (T-052–T-056).
Integration must verify these contracts in ProviderCore/Addon/{AddonIPCServer,AddonPeerPolicy,AddonHoldPaths,ProviderLoop+AddonHold}.swift: request-time authentication across exec, safe filesystem/socket replacement, bounded client resource use, persistence validation, lock lifecycle and admission reopening only after proven native retirement. Cross-check holds against cancellation, model switching, shutdown, retained native faults and coordinator busy/routing behavior (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, T-010, T-028, T-029, T-053). The implementation is not supplied here, so documentation is not proof of those controls. The reference cites new TB-012 at line 97, absent from the BASE index; reconcile the PR's threat-model update for the same-user add-on/VM boundary and lock-driven availability effects. Unchanged configuration context does not itself demonstrate regressions.
